- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast shows strong downward bias, increase forecast by 2–5% to avoid pessimism.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a recent spike, reduce peak by 10–15% to account for mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward trend, model should not overshoot below recent lows.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7) and forecast is erratic, smooth transitions by averaging 2–3 prior values before next step.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true values by 3–5% over 3–5 days, apply a 3–5% downward correction to future steps.  
- If sentiment is rising (increasing over last 5 days) and forecast is flat or declining, adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect momentum.
